findings.evidence: Lines 94-95: `rai = p;` / `connected = true;` cache the provider's table pointer. The only code that clears `rai`/`connected` is `init()` (lines 71-72). Nothing re-validates or drops the cached pointer afterwards, and `poll()` (line 100) returns early once `connected` is true, so `require()` is never called again.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check how KPatchApi::require() hands out K2RangedAiApi (static table in the provider DLL vs. heap). Then check whether any consumer of k2rai::Client (companion AI A1 hook, ranged-ai provider) calls init() on DLL unload or reload, and whether a provider unload can happen while a consumer is still running. kpatch_api.h is not in the packet and was not found under _shared_src, so the require() signature and lifetime rules could not be verified here.
findings.why_it_matters: If the ranged-ai provider DLL is unloaded or hot-swapped (the KPM install/hot-swap path), a consumer that keeps this Client alive will call KiteStance/MapsToRanged through a dangling function-pointer table. The header has no disconnect or revalidation step to prevent that.
